question:
In which of the following parts of India Monsoon Trough encourage(s) the development of thermal low?

A. North India

B. South India

C. Northwest India

D. Northeast India
solution:
The correct answer is __**A and C**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The development of a thermal low across north and northwest India is encouraged by this **monsoon trough.**
 
• The southern hemisphere's trade winds begin to blow from the southwest to the northeast due to the **Coriolis force **as a result of the **ITCZ's shift**, which occurs between **40° and 60°E longitudes.**
 
• Southwest monsoon develops. When the Indian **ITCZ** is placed to the north in July, it causes the Monsoon Trough, which is significant because it affects the Indian monsoon. **This promotes the formation of a thermal low over northern and western India.**
 
• The southern hemisphere's trade winds now cross the equator as a result of this ITCZ change.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monsoon Trough**

 
 
• As seen by a line on a weather map showing the places of minimum sea level pressure, the** monsoon trough** is a component of the **Intertropical Convergence Zone** in the Western Pacific and is, thus, a **convergence zone** between the wind patterns of the southern and northern hemispheres.
 
• Easterly trade winds exist poleward of the trough, whereas westerly monsoon winds are located in its **equatorward region.**
 
• **Heavy rains** that signal the height of any place's rainy season can be located right along its axis.
 
• Climate conditions become hot and dry when it moves poleward of a site. Many of the world's rainforests are influenced by the monsoon trough.
